slides.title: Buyers trust proof before they trust [chemistry].
slides.lede: A high-stakes buyer must believe you can do the work, will do the work, and will act responsibly when the work becomes difficult.

items.title: Competence
items.text: Can this supplier solve the problem?

items.title: Consistency
items.text: Will the experience match the promise?

items.title: Dependability
items.text: Will they meet commitments under pressure?

cards.label: Low trust
cards.text: The buyer lacks evidence. Provide it.

cards.label: Distrust
cards.text: The buyer doubts your motives. More promotional proof may worsen it.

slides.title: Swap vague promises for [things a buyer can check]
slides.note: Buyers trust suppliers that can describe **both the upside and the boundaries** of an engagement.

slides.title: Watch what buyers [risk], not just what they say
slides.text: Track stakeholder access, approval delays, scope disputes, renewal quality and willingness to refer. A buyer may renew because switching is costly, while still withholding strategic information.

items.title: State the failure plainly
items.text: No vague language for the buyer to decode.

items.title: Explain the operational impact
items.text: What changed and who is affected.

items.title: Present a credible recovery plan
items.text: Named owners, dates and decision points.

items.title: Change the system
items.text: Show the fix that reduces recurrence.

items.title: Verify recovery with the buyer
items.text: Do not assume confidence has returned.

slides.title: Make trust visible wherever the buyer takes a risk.
slides.lede: B2B trust formation: how high-stakes buyers decide to rely on you. Read the full guide via the link in our bio.
